::: {#exm-count-walks}
#### Walks in the office graph

With the adjacency matrix $A_G$ of @exm-adjacency-matrix, in the order $a, b, c, d, e, f$,

$$
A_G^2 =
\begin{bmatrix}
2 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 0
\\
1 & 3 & 1 & 0 & 2 & 1
\\
1 & 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 & 1
\\
1 & 0 & 2 & 3 & 1 & 1
\\
1 & 2 & 0 & 1 & 3 & 1
\\
0 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 & 2
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

By @thm-count-walks, there are 2 walks of length 2 from $b$ to $e$ (row 2, column 5): $b, c, e$ and $b, d, e$.
In a simple graph (@def-simple-graph) such as this one, the diagonal entries are the degrees (@def-degree),
since a walk of length 2 from $v$ back to $v$ goes out to a neighbor and comes back along the same edge.

The entry of $A_G^3$ in row 1 and column 6 is 2:
the walks of length 3 from $a$ to $f$ are $a, b, d, f$ and $a, c, e, f$.

:::
